newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF head says time to resume lending to Russia.
newsitem.headline: IMF head says time to resume lending to Russia.

text.p: The head of the International Monetary Fund, holding out the prospect of Western inflation levels in Russia, said on Wednesday the time was right for the fund to resume lending to Moscow to back its economic reforms.

IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus reminded students at an international affairs institute that the fund had granted Russia a $10 billion three-year Extended Fund Facility Loan last year, when conditions were less certain than today.
"Why would we shy away now from continuing extending our support to Russia?" he asked.

"This is also the time for us, in the international community, to go ahead with our support for the completion of your reforms... by resuming our financing and risking our resources once again in support of your programme: a signal the markets expect, a signal your programme deserves," he said.
The IMF has repeatedly suspended monthly payments of the loan because it fears that Russian tax revenues, running well below budgeted levels, could undermine Russia's finances.
"Yes, the crisis of non-payments of taxes is serious," Camdessus said.
Camdessus is in Moscow for talks with senior Russian ministers on resuming disbursements and agreeing an economic programme for 1997 to be backed by the loan.
Camdessus called on the authorities to boost tax revenues by forcing the biggest debtors to pay up. He also appealed for reform of the tax system and the elimination of corruption.
But he said the economy was making progress, and inflation could fall below 10 percent next year.
"Stabilisation is proceeding in a remarkable way," he said. If reforms continue "next year you will have the single-digit inflation of the other industrial countries".
The government is targeting annual inflation this year of about 12 percent after 22 percent in 1996.
